1.note: Zechariah is using the words translated as **The burden of the word of Yahweh concerning Israel** to introduce a new event in the story. Use a word, phrase, or other method in your language that is natural for introducing a new event.

Here Zechariah is speaking of the message from Yahweh as if it were a **burden**, that is, a heavy load that a person must carry. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [The severe word of Yahweh]

Zechariah is using **the declaration of Yahweh** to indicate that what has been said is a direct quotation from Yahweh and comes with Yahweh’s authority. In your translation, use a natural way of indicating direct quotations in your language.

Here Zechariah is speaking of how Yahweh made the world as if he were **stretching out** a tent to form the heavens and **founding** a building to form the earth. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [the one who made the heavens and who made the earth]

This phrase continues the references to creation. The **spirit** of man represents “life.” The word translated **man** could also be transliterated as “Adam.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [the life of a person] or [Adam’s life]

2.note: This is the beginning of what Yahweh said. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could mark that this is a direct quote of Yahweh.

Zechariah is using the term **Behold** to focus his listeners’ attention on what he is about to say. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation. Alternate translation: [Listen]

Here Yahweh is speaking of **Jerusalem** as if it were a **cup of staggering**, that is, a cup of wine that would make the surrounding nations drunk so that they reel and cannot stand. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [a source of helpless reeling for all of the peoples all around]

This could mean: (1) Judah and Jerusalem are besieged. Alternate translation: [And just as Jerusalem is besieged, so is all of Judah.] (2) Judah is going to besiege Jerusalem. Alternate translation: [Judah joins the nations to besiege Jerusalem.]

3.note: Here Yahweh is speaking of Jerusalem as if it were a **stone of burden**, that is, a stone so heavy that anyone who tries to lift it injures himself. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [a burden too heavy for all of the peoples]

Yahweh is repeating forms of the verb **injuring** in order to intensify his expression of the idea that it conveys. If your language can repeat words for intensification, it would be appropriate to do that here in your translation. If not, your language may have another way of expressing the intensification. Alternate translation: [will certainly be severely injured]

Yahweh is using the participle **the ones lifting it** as a noun to mean a certain kind of person, namely, the nations who try to take Jerusalem for themselves. Your language may use participles in the same way. If not, you can translate this participle with an equivalent phrase. Alternate translation: [All of the nations who try to lift it]

The expression **will be injured** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [will surely injure themselves severely]

The expression **will be gathered** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [and all of the nations of the earth will assemble themselves against it]

4.note: If your language does not use abstract nouns for the ideas of **confusion** and **madness**, you could express the same ideas in other ways. Alternate translation: [I will strike every horse so that it becomes bewildered and its rider so that he becomes crazed]

Here Yahweh is speaking of the people of Judah as if they were a **house**, a single household. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [the Judean people]

Yahweh is using **I will open my eyes** as a common expression of the culture to mean “I will watch over and protect.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [I will keep watch protectively]

4.q: כָל־סוּס֙ בַּ⁠תִּמָּה֔וֹן וְ⁠רֹכְב֖⁠וֹ בַּ⁠שִּׁגָּע֑וֹן & וְ⁠כֹל֙ ס֣וּס הָֽ⁠עַמִּ֔ים
4.note: Yahweh is using **every horse**, **every horse of the peoples**, and **its rider** to represent the whole army of the enemy nations. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression from your culture or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [all the enemy forces with confusion and their soldiers with madness … every horse of the enemy]

5.note: Zechariah is using **will say in their heart** as a common expression of the culture to mean “will say to themselves” or “will think.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Then the chiefs of Judah will think to themselves]

5.q: אַמְצָ֥ה לִ⁠י֙ יֹשְׁבֵ֣י יְרוּשָׁלִַ֔ם בַּ⁠יהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת אֱלֹהֵי⁠הֶֽם
5.note: The words that the chiefs of Judah say are a quotation within Yahweh’s quotation. If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [that the dwellers of Jerusalem are strength for them through Yahweh of Armies, their God]

This could mean: (1) the people who live in Jerusalem are strong because Yahweh of Armies their God is with them or (2) the people who live in Jerusalem are a source of strength for the chiefs of Judah. You could make this information explicit if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [The dwellers of Jerusalem are a source of strength to me]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **strength**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [strengthen me]

The pronoun **me** is singular, referring to each chief of Judah individually, even though all the chiefs are speaking. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [to each of us]

6.q: כְּֽ⁠כִיּ֧וֹר אֵ֣שׁ בְּ⁠עֵצִ֗ים וּ⁠כְ⁠לַפִּ֥יד אֵשׁ֙ בְּ⁠עָמִ֔יר
6.note: The point of this comparison is that just as **a basin of fire among trees** and **a torch of fire in a sheaf** quickly burn up everything around them, so the chiefs of Judah will destroy the peoples around them. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [able to consume their enemies as quickly as a firepot burns up wood and as a flaming torch burns up a sheaf of grain]

A **basin** is a kind of large, open container that can hold burning coals or fire. If your readers would not be familiar with what a basin of this kind is, you could use the name of a similar thing that your readers would recognize, or you could use a more general term. Alternate translation: [like a pot full of burning coals]

A **sheaf** is a bundle of cut grain stalks tied together. When dried, it is highly flammable. If your readers would not be familiar with what a sheaf is, you could use a more general term or explain it in a footnote. Alternate translation: [bundle of cut grain]

Here Yahweh is speaking of the chiefs of Judah destroying their enemies as if they would **devour** them the way fire consumes what it burns. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and they will destroy]

Yahweh is referring to every direction by naming two major components, **the right** and **the left**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [in every direction]

Here, **Jerusalem** represents the people who live in Jerusalem. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [And the people of Jerusalem will dwell again in their place]

It might seem that the expression **in its place, in Jerusalem** contains extra information that would not be natural to express in your language. If so, you could shorten it. Alternate translation: [in its own place]

7.note: Here, **so that** marks **the honor of the house of David and the honor of the dweller of Jerusalem will not be great over Judah** as the goal or purpose of Yahweh saving the tents of Judah first. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that this is the purpose. Alternate translation: [in order that]

Here, **the tents of Judah** represents the homes and households of the people of Judah. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [the households of Judah]

If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **honor**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the honored house of David and the honored dweller of Jerusalem]

Here Zechariah is speaking of the descendants of King David, the royal family, as if they were a **house**, a single household. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [the royal family descended from David]

Zechariah is not referring to a specific **dweller** of Jerusalem. He means the people who live in Jerusalem in general. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use an expression that would be more natural in your language. Alternate translation: [the residents of Jerusalem]

7.q: לֹֽא־תִגְדַּ֜ל תִּפְאֶ֣רֶת בֵּית־דָּוִ֗יד וְ⁠תִפְאֶ֛רֶת יֹשֵׁ֥ב יְרוּשָׁלִַ֖ם עַל־יְהוּדָֽה
7.note: Zechariah is using **will not be great over Judah** as a common expression of the culture to mean “will not be considered more important than the rest of Judah.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [the honor of the house of David and the honor of the dweller of Jerusalem will not be regarded as more important than the honor of the rest of Judah]

8.note: Here Zechariah is speaking of a weak or feeble person as if he were a **stumbler**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and the weakest one among them]

Zechariah is using the adjective **stumbler** as a noun to mean a certain kind of person. Your language may use adjectives in the same way. If not, you can translate this adjective with an equivalent phrase. Alternate translation: [the one who stumbles]

Zechariah says **will be like David, and the house of David, like God** as an extreme statement for emphasis. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use a different way to express the emphasis. Alternate translation: [will be strong like David was, and the house of David will seem as powerful as God]

Zechariah is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. It may be helpful to repeat them from the earlier phrase. Alternate translation: [and the house of David will be like God]

The point of this comparison is that just as **God** and **the angel of Yahweh** are powerful, so the house of David will be powerful as they lead the people. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [and the house of David will be as powerful as God is, as powerful as the angel of Yahweh]

Here, **their face** represents their presence, so the phrase means going ahead of the people to lead them. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [like having the angel of Yahweh fighting in front of them]

9.q: וְ⁠הָיָ֖ה בַּ⁠יּ֣וֹם הַ⁠ה֑וּא אֲבַקֵּ֗שׁ לְ⁠הַשְׁמִיד֙ אֶת־כָּל־הַ⁠גּוֹיִ֔ם הַ⁠בָּאִ֖ים עַל־יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם
9.note: Here Yahweh’s direct speech resumes after the narration of the previous verses. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could mark that this is a direct quote of Yahweh.

10.note: Here Yahweh is speaking of generously giving his spirit to people as if he would **pour out** a liquid on them. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And I will generously bestow]

If your language does not use abstract nouns for the ideas of **favor** and **supplications**, you could express the same ideas in other ways. Alternate translation: [a spirit that causes me to be pleased with them to plead with me and causes me to be pleased with them]

10.q: וְ⁠הִבִּ֥יטוּ אֵלַ֖⁠י אֵ֣ת אֲשֶׁר־דָּקָ֑רוּ וְ⁠סָפְד֣וּ עָלָ֗י⁠ו
10.note: The pronoun **him** refers to the same person as **me** earlier in the verse. Yahweh shifts here from speaking of himself in the first person to speaking of the pierced one in the third person. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [and they will look to me, whom they pierced. And they will mourn over the one they pierced]

The point of this comparison is that just as people grieve very deeply for **the only one**, that is, an only child who has died, so the people will mourn over the one whom they pierced. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [And they will mourn over him as deeply as people grieve for an only child who has died]

The point of this comparison is that just as people grieve bitterly over **the firstborn**, that is, a firstborn son who has died, so the people will grieve bitterly over the one whom they pierced. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [and they will weep powerfully over him, just as people weep powerfully when a firstborn son dies]

11.note: The point of this comparison is that just as **the mourning of Hadad Rimmon in the plain of Megiddo** was a well-known time of very great grief, so the mourning in Jerusalem will be very great. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [as great as the well-known grief at Hadad Rimmon in the plain of Megiddo]

This could mean: (1) the weeping for King Josiah, who was killed at Megiddo and for whom the people mourned greatly, Alternate translation: [like the mourning for King Josiah at Hadad Rimmon] or (2) the ritual mourning for a god named Hadad Rimmon, or (3) both. You could include this information in a footnote if that would be helpful to your readers.
The word **Hadad Rimmon** is the name of a place, and the word **Megiddo** is the name of a place.

12.note: In some languages, the repeated systematic repetition of the rest of verse 12 through verse 14 may not give a similar emphasis to the deepness and powerfulness of the mourning that will happen. Translate in a way that emphasizes how strong the grief was in a natural way in your language. Alternate translation: [the clans of David, Nathan, Levi, and the Shimeite will all mourn very intensely; the men and women will mourn separately, in their own ways]

Zechariah assumes that readers will know that the separation of men and women in public mourning reflects the mourning customs of that society. Translate this so readers do not misinterpret it as marital strife or divorce. You could say that explicitly if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [According to custom, each clan will mourn by itself, and men and women will mourn separately]

Here, **the land** represents the people who live in the land. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [And everyone living in the land will mourn]

Zechariah is repeating the term **clans** in order to intensify his expression of the idea that it conveys, that each clan mourns by itself. If your language can repeat words for intensification, it would be appropriate to do that here in your translation. If not, your language may have another way of expressing the intensification. Alternate translation: [each and every clan will mourn separately]

12.q: מִשְׁפַּ֨חַת בֵּית־דָּוִ֤יד לְ⁠בָד֙ וּ⁠נְשֵׁי⁠הֶ֣ם לְ⁠בָ֔ד מִשְׁפַּ֤חַת בֵּית־נָתָן֙ לְ⁠בָ֔ד וּ⁠נְשֵׁי⁠הֶ֖ם לְ⁠בָֽד
12.note: Zechariah is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [The men of the clan of the house of David will mourn by themselves and the women of that clan will mourn by themselves. The men of the clan descended from Nathan will mourn by themselves and the women of that clan will mourn by themselves]

This could mean: (1) Nathan, the son of King David, Alternate translation: [the house of Nathan, David’s son] or (2) Nathan, the prophet who served during David’s reign. Alternate translation: [the house of prophet Nathan] You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers.

13.note: The word **Shimeite** is the name of a people group, the descendants of a man named Shimei.

14.note: Zechariah is using the adjective **the ones remaining** as a noun to mean certain clans, namely, all the other clans that have not yet been named. Your language may use adjectives in the same way. If not, you can translate this adjective with an equivalent phrase. Alternate translation: [and any other clans]
